title: Tokenizing characters vs. subwords vs. words

cues.en: The upshot of this video is the following.
cues.zh: 這支影片的重點如下。

cues.en: Tokenization schemes based purely at the character level have some advantages, but more disadvantages.
cues.zh: 純字元層級的斷詞方案有一些優點，但缺點更多。

cues.en: And the same goes for tokenizing entire words.
cues.zh: 以整個單字斷詞，也有同樣情況。

cues.en: And it turns out that subwords, which are parts of words, is an optimal balance between the pros and
cues.zh: 而子詞，也就是單字的一部分，能在字元斷詞與整詞斷詞的

cues.en: the cons of tokenizing characters versus entire words.
cues.zh: 優缺點之間，取得最佳平衡。

cues.en: So let me start by reminding you of some terminology.
cues.zh: 先複習一些術語。

cues.en: This is a slide that you saw several videos ago.
cues.zh: 這張投影片，你在幾支影片前看過。

cues.en: And the idea is that we need to translate text into integers.
cues.zh: 概念是，必須把文字轉成整數。

cues.en: And tokenization is the process of segmenting text so that it can be represented using numbers.
cues.zh: 斷詞就是切分文字，讓它能以數字表示的過程。

cues.en: We can segment based on individual characters like letters and numbers and punctuation marks.
cues.zh: 可以依個別字元切分，例如字母、數字與標點符號。

cues.en: Or we can assign a number to each individual word and then subwords are somewhere in the middle.
cues.zh: 也可以為每個完整單字指定數字，而子詞則介於兩者之間。

cues.en: So here you see a list of advantages in green and disadvantages in red of character level tokenization.
cues.zh: 這裡列出字元層級斷詞的優點與缺點，分別以綠色與紅色表示。

cues.en: Basically, character level tokenization has a very small vocabulary that is easily adapted to any language and also any misspellings of words.
cues.zh: 基本上，字元斷詞的詞彙表很小，容易適應任何語言，以及任何拼字錯誤。

cues.en: On the other hand, each token conveys little semantic meaning, so that means that training a language
cues.zh: 另一方面，每個 token 傳達的語意很少，因此訓練語言

cues.en: model would require a lot more data and a lot more expensive compute time.
cues.zh: 模型需要更多資料，以及更昂貴的計算時間。

cues.en: Character based tokenization schemes also limit the length of the sequences that the language model
cues.zh: 字元斷詞也會限制語言模型能處理的

cues.en: can process, which means that the language models won't be as good.
cues.zh: 序列長度，使語言模型的表現較差。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: And then we have the word based tokenization schemes.
cues.zh: 接著是以單字為基礎的斷詞方案。

cues.en: And the main advantage here is that each token corresponds to a semantically meaningful and also human
cues.zh: 主要優點是，每個 token 都對應一段有語意、而且人類

cues.en: interpretable piece of text, which also means that it's easier and faster for a language model to learn
cues.zh: 能解讀的文字；這也代表語言模型能更容易、更快速地學習

cues.en: associations between words, and also to have a longer context window.
cues.zh: 單字之間的關聯，也能擁有更長的上下文視窗。

cues.en: But it requires a large vocabulary, and that vocabulary would increase enormously for each additional language that we want the model to be able to understand.
cues.zh: 但它需要很大的詞彙表，而且每增加一種模型要理解的語言，詞彙表就會大幅增加。

cues.en: This term here stands for out of vocabulary.
cues.zh: 這個術語代表 out of vocabulary，也就是詞彙表之外。

cues.en: This basically refers to unusual words or low frequency words, and also misspellings of words.
cues.zh: 基本上，指的是罕見、低頻的單字，以及拼字錯誤。

cues.en: So just imagine if we would need a separate token for every possible misspelling of every possible word that we want the model to recognize.
cues.zh: 想像一下，如果希望模型辨識的每個單字，每一種可能的錯誤拼法，都需要一個獨立 token。

cues.en: And also we would need to have double tokens for words that are spelled differently in, for example, American English versus British English.
cues.zh: 此外，像美式與英式英文拼法不同的單字，也需要兩個 token。

cues.en: Anyway, you can see that these two you can see these two as extremes on this spectrum.
cues.zh: 總之，可以把這兩種方式，看成這個光譜的兩個極端。

cues.en: And then of course we have sub words in the middle.
cues.zh: 子詞當然就位在中間。

cues.en: So a subword tokenization finds a nice balance between the pros and cons of smaller and larger segmentations of text.
cues.zh: 所以，子詞斷詞能在較小與較大的文字切分單位之間，取得良好的優缺點平衡。

cues.en: Now to be clear, subword based tokenization also includes individual characters and entire words.
cues.zh: 說清楚一點，以子詞為基礎的斷詞，也包含單一字元與完整單字。

cues.en: So it's not that these two extremes are excluded, it's just that the tokenizer is optimized for letter sequences.
cues.zh: 並不是排除這兩個極端，只是 tokenizer 針對字母序列進行最佳化，

cues.en: It's not optimized for individual characters or entire words.
cues.zh: 而不是針對個別字元或完整單字最佳化。

cues.en: But you do end up with individual characters and you end up with full words.
cues.zh: 但最終仍會出現個別字元，也會出現完整單字。

cues.en: Okay, this slide shows a table.
cues.zh: 這張投影片是一個表格，

cues.en: That's basically just another way of representing what I discussed in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 基本上，只是用另一種方式呈現上一張投影片的內容。

cues.en: And yeah, all the green text are advantages and the red text are disadvantages.
cues.zh: 綠色文字都是優點，紅色文字都是缺點。

cues.en: So yeah, I don't have anything really new to discuss here except to say that character based and word based tokenization schemes are good for some things, they're not so good for other things.
cues.zh: 所以，這裡沒有太多新內容；只是說明字元斷詞與整詞斷詞各有所長，也各有不足。

cues.en: And subword based approaches are designed to be somewhere in the middle.
cues.zh: 而子詞方法，設計上就是要介於兩者之間。

cues.en: So for the rest of this section, and also the rest of this course, we are only going to be working with subword based tokenization schemes.
cues.zh: 因此，這一章後面，以及整門課接下來，都只使用以子詞為基礎的斷詞方案。

cues.en: The current most popular and best tokenization scheme for Llms is called byte pair encoding.
cues.zh: 目前 LLM 最常見、最好的斷詞方案，稱為位元組配對編碼，byte pair encoding。

cues.en: And I'm going to introduce you to that algorithm in the next video.
cues.zh: 下一支影片會介紹這個演算法。
